exposure: Unit policy regarding mode of delivery (systematic CS, no policy, vaginal delivery)
outcome: Moderate to severe neurodevelopmental impairment at 2 years of corrected age
cohort: Singleton vertex-presenting live births at 24 + 0 to 31 + 6 weeks of gestation without serious congenital anomalies, preeclampsia, HELLP or eclampsia, antenatal detection of growth restriction and prelabour CS for fetal or maternal indications
finding: Among singleton vertex-presenting live births without medical complications requiring a CS at 24 + 0 to 31 + 6 weeks of gestation, cesarean section was not associated with improved neonatal or long-term outcomes.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was not associated with improved composite outcome of in-hospital mortality and intraventricular haemorrhage or periventricular leukomalacia, or with neurodevelopmental impairment at two years of age.
